notes.title: Free DLC "Fishing The Abyss AQUARIUM" is Now Available!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, it's been a while.

Thanks to your incredible support, Fishing The Abyss has been purchased and reviewed by many players. As my first release as a solo developer, this experience has been full of learning and growth for me.

I truly appreciate all the feedback you've provided.
(And of course, I’ll always be happy to receive more reviews in the future.)

As a token of my gratitude, I'm pleased to announce the release of a free downloadable content, Fishing The Abyss AQUARIUM.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318139/03700082c08c2a28acd3ad1ee6d72749ede83f6a.png[/img]

This DLC was created both to fulfill requests from players who wanted to view the entire bodies of the creatures, and to express my appreciation to those who continue playing far longer than I ever anticipated.

Fishing The Abyss AQUARIUM is a standalone DLC that launches independently from the main game.

Note: Launching it together with the main game requires a few additional steps. Please refer to the bottom section of the DLC’s store page for details.

To display the full bodies of the creatures, it was necessary to use a 16:9 screen ratio.

Making it a standalone DLC allowed me to implement this feature, although it might feel quite different from the main game and cause some confusion at first.

For more details, please check the store page or simply try it out—it’s free to download and enjoy. Key features include:

A gallery mode that allows you to carefully observe each creature’s full body

Integration with your save data: record and store the sizes of the creatures you've caught

Register saved creatures in an aquarium and enjoy watching them swim

Feed your favorite creatures to make them larger—or smaller, if you prefer

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318139/523af455fed891c7ab86253b2e2bdf0e3fcfe593.png[/img]

If you’re a player with a large collection of catches, I hope you'll enjoy crafting your own personalized aquarium.
For new players, combining this DLC with the main game from the start might offer a fresh and enjoyable experience.

Alongside the DLC release, the main game has also been updated to version 1.4.1.

This update mainly includes support for the new DLC and some bug fixes:

Fixes:

When the music window was open, the loop toggle button overlapped with the rain control button, causing frequent misclicks. This has been fixed by disabling rain controls while the music window is open.

Fixed an issue where both loop and random playback could be activated simultaneously upon loading a save file.

There are still some music-related issues that have been reported, but I’ve been unable to reproduce them in the development environment. As such, they are not fixed in this update.

I also wanted to implement cloud saving, as requested by many of you.
However, during testing, I found a critical risk: if the initial sync occurs in a version with cloud saving enabled, it may overwrite local save data with an empty cloud state—essentially wiping existing saves.
While there are workarounds, the potential for irreversible data loss was too great if anything went wrong, so I’ve decided to withhold this feature.

If I release another title in the future, I plan to support cloud saving from the beginning. But for Fishing The Abyss, cloud saving will not be implemented.

I sincerely apologize for this decision and ask for your understanding.

Thank you again for your continued support of Fishing The Abyss and the brand new DLC, Fishing The Abyss AQUARIUM.

notes.title: Ver 1.4.0 Beta Update
notes.notes:
We have added new items to the system save data and implemented additional features utilizing Windows functionality. To distinguish this from an official version update, we have decided to release it as a Beta version.

[h2]The previous Beta version had no reported issues and has been adopted as the official version.[/h2]

[h1]Update Details[/h1]

[h3]・Added an option to keep the window always on top.[/h3]

Note 1: Windows OS only
Note 2: Not available in borderless window mode; it can only be used in windowed mode.

[h1]How to Update to the Beta Version[/h1]

Note: The Beta version is a test version that may include potential bugs due to major updates or other changes.
While we have conducted internal testing before release, please refrain from updating if you are concerned about possible issues.

[h3]1: Right-click on the title "Fishing The Abyss" in your Steam library to display a pop-up menu.

2: Open the "Properties" menu.

3: Select "Beta" and set the drop-down menu under "Participation in beta" to "beta - beta version build," then close the window.

4: The update will proceed automatically (if it does not start automatically, please click the update button manually). Once you see "[beta]" added to the title, the update is complete.[/h3]

If you wish to revert to the official version, follow step 3 and select "None" instead of the Beta option.

notes.title: ver 1.3.0 Beta Update
notes.notes:
This update introduces a critical data protection system for save data, so we have decided to release it as a [b]Beta version, separate from the official update[/b].

[h1]Update Details[/h1]

[h3]・Implemented a system to detect data corruption caused by interruptions during save data writing and automatically recover from backup data.[/h3]

With this feature, the folder icon previously displayed on the title screen has been removed. In the unlikely event of save data corruption, players will no longer need to manually restore save data from a backup.

[h3]・The reset button in the settings screen now resets the window scale and height to their minimum values, moves the window to the zero position (top-left corner) of the display, and initializes it.[/h3]

This adjustment addresses an issue where players with low-resolution displays could not adjust the vertical height of the window, providing a solution for such cases.

[h3]・Added a time limit to the popup confirmation for transitioning to the ending replay after clearing the game.[/h3]

This update improves a situation where players had to interact with the ending replay popup unnecessarily if they did not adjust depth after clearing the game. A countdown of approximately five seconds will appear in the popup, after which it will close automatically, and players will return to fishing. If you wish to view the ending replay, please press the OK button during the countdown.

[h3]・The game now performs an achievement unlock check every time you load a game if the conditions for unlocking achievements are met.[/h3]

This is an enhancement of a previous update. While most achievements were addressed, some remained unhandled. This version ensures all achievements are covered.

[h3]Updates automatically applied separately from ver 1.3.0 Beta[/h3]

Corrected the wording for hidden conditions of some achievements.

[h1]How to Update to the Beta Version[/h1]

Note: The Beta version is a test build that may contain potential bugs due to major updates. Although internal testing has been conducted, please refrain from updating if you are concerned about encountering issues.

[h3]1. In your Steam library, right-click on the "Fishing The Abyss" title to display the pop-up menu.

2. Open the "Properties" menu.

3. Select the "Beta" tab, then choose "beta - Beta version build" from the drop-down menu under "Opt into Beta," and close the window.

4. The update will be applied automatically (if it does not proceed automatically, please press the Update button manually). Confirm that "[beta]" has been added to the title name to complete the process.[/h3]

If you want to revert from the Beta version to the official version, follow step 3 and select "None" instead of Beta.

Note: Automatic translation may result in slight differences in wording from the original text.

notes.title: Refund Request Guidance for Customers Affected by the ver 1.1.0 Point Accumulati
notes.notes:
Hello, this is umaaaaaa, the developer of Fishing The Abyss.

First and foremost, I would like to sincerely apologize once again for the inconvenience caused by the issue in ver 1.1.0, where starting the game from either "New Game" or "Continue" resulted in beginning with an excessive amount of points.

Although the issue was resolved with the release of version 1.1.1 just a few hours later, it still affected both new purchasers during that time and existing players who had already been enjoying the game.

After reaching out to Steam Support and providing a detailed explanation of how this issue impacted players, I negotiated with them to accommodate refund requests beyond the usual refund conditions. As a result, they have agreed to approve refunds for customers who purchased the game before the ver 1.1.1 patch and can explain the issue they encountered.

If you would like to request a refund, please follow the instructions below to submit your refund request and await Steam's decision. I deeply regret asking for your time and effort in this process, but I sincerely appreciate your understanding.

[h2][b]Please note: Customers who purchased the game starting from version 1.1.1 or later are not eligible for a refund.[/b][/h2]

[olist]
[h1][*]Steam Support URL[/h1]
https://help.steampowered.com/
Please access this page.

[h2][b]Steps:[/b][/h2]

[*]Click on the "Purchases" button.

[*]A list of your purchase history will appear. Find "Fishing The Abyss" in the list and click on it.

[*]Click the "I would like a refund" button.

[*]Next, click the "I’d like to request a refund" button.

[*]You may see a message indicating that your purchase does not meet the refund conditions. However, there will be a text box at the bottom labeled "Notes." Please select "It’s not listed here" as the reason and provide a detailed explanation of your situation.

[*]Finally, click the "Submit Request" button at the bottom, and wait for Steam Support to contact you via the registered email address.
[/olist]

That’s all for the instructions. Thank you for your effort, and I sincerely hope your refund request will be approved.

If any eligible customers are denied a refund by Steam Support due to insufficient justification, I truly apologize. I regret that I cannot do more in such cases, but I will take this experience to heart and ensure that it informs both my future development and operations to prevent such issues from occurring again. Thank you for your understanding.

A note from the developer:
At the time of writing this, I have received very few direct refund requests. On the contrary, many customers have reached out with messages of forgiveness, for which I am incredibly grateful.

However, I also believe there may have been some customers who chose not to speak up, paying for the game but not enjoying it due to the inconvenience caused by this issue.

As an independent developer releasing my first game, I deeply appreciate the understanding and kindness shown by everyone. At the same time, I want to do everything possible to avoid the perception of abandoning players after a sale. (Even though I understand that some degree of dissatisfaction is unavoidable when selling products widely.)

My ultimate goal is to deliver value that exceeds the price you paid for the game. Thank you for your continued support, and I will strive to make this a reality.

Sincerely,
umaaaaaa
---------------------------------------------------

[h2]Additional Notice

This refund process will have a deadline of "two weeks, including the date of this announcement."
If there are any eligible individuals who have not yet submitted their request, please ensure that your request is completed within the deadline.[/h2]

notes.title: ver 1.2.0：UpDate
notes.notes:
[b]Update[/b]

[b][h2]Switch Functionality: Always Rain ←→ Auto (Default Behavior)[/h2][/b]
This feature is available from the start of the game.
To activate, left-click on a ground lamp during gameplay; a faint light will turn on.
When the light is on, rain will continue to fall endlessly. Turning off the light will revert the behavior to the default, alternating naturally between rain and sunshine.

[b][h2]New Mini Icon for the Encyclopedia: Displayed When a New Creature is Caught[/h2][/b]
Previously, you had to open the encyclopedia to know if you had caught a new creature.
With this update, an orange mini-icon will appear on the encyclopedia icon, letting you know before opening it.

[b][h2]Added Max Level Rewards and Conditions for "Reel Performance" and "Weight"[/h2][/b]
Descriptions now include details about max level rewards and unlock conditions from the start.
This change was made to address the hesitation players felt about leveling up, as increasing the level enhanced sinking and floating speeds, which conflicted with the slower, scenic fishing style some players preferred.
The explanation was added since it was originally harmless to reveal this information early.

Initially, we considered adding a level adjustment feature right from the start. However, to maintain the simplicity of gameplay and mouse-only controls, we decided against implementing this feature alongside the leveling process, as it would make the system more complex. Instead, level adjustment becomes available after reaching the level cap, allowing the left mouse button—freed from its level-up role—to manage level adjustments.
While adding a button was an option, we prioritized minimal button use wherever possible.

With this update, we hope you’ll feel free to level up without worry, though you might need to endure faster background scrolling for a while. Rest assured that once you reach the max level, this restriction will be lifted—so level up boldly!

[b][h2]Automatic Save Data Backup System[/h2][/b]
In ver1.1.0, a bug that allowed excessive point acquisition caused inconvenience for many players.
As save data was stored locally with no recovery options, players had no way to restore lost data.

To address this, an automatic backup system has been introduced to mitigate issues caused by data loss due to local environment factors.
If recovery is necessary, players can manually access the backup folder and move or overwrite the data. While this requires manual action, it significantly improves the recovery situation compared to complete data loss.

Hovering over the folder icon added to the title screen displays the local save data path and additional details.
Note: The default save location is in the hidden AppData folder. Please enable the display of hidden files in the folder options to access it.

[b][h2]Steam Overlay Screenshot Feature: Default Key F12[/h2][/b]

[b][h2]Miscellaneous Bug Fixes[/h2][/b]

notes.title: ver 1.1.1 Fixed an Issue Where the Game Started with Abnormal Point Values
notes.notes:
ssue Identified in ver1.1.0!

We have confirmed a critical issue in ver1.1.0 where the game starts with an abnormal point value. This is a serious problem that should never have occurred...

We have now released ver1.1.1 to address this issue. However, I deeply apologize to the 74 players who purchased the game during the time ver1.1.0 was available and those who started playing during this period. Unfortunately, they experienced a flawed gameplay experience that did not meet expectations.

For players unable to obtain a refund through Steam's refund system, I am currently exploring solutions (I am committed to issuing refunds where appropriate and am investigating the best way to handle this situation).

I am sincerely sorry for the inconvenience caused by this issue. Rest assured that I will handle this matter with the utmost sincerity and care.

Currently, I am in contact with Steam Support to inquire whether refunds can be processed through Steam’s system.
[strike]If this is not possible, I am also considering issuing refunds individually. However, since the developer, Uma, is an individual, I am carefully exploring methods to ensure the process does not involve exchanging personal information or cause any disadvantages to the players.[/strike]

As a result of our investigation, we have determined that it would be problematic for an individual developer to provide refunds outside of Steam’s official system. For the time being, we kindly ask for your patience while we await a response from Steam Support regarding this matter.

Thank you for your patience and understanding.

umaaaaaa

--------------------------------------------------------------
Additional Note: Cause of the Issue and Countermeasures

Upon investigating the cause of the issue, we discovered that it was due to a long-unused debugging feature that remained in the build with its switch turned on. While we identified the problem, we had conducted debugging before releasing the version, so it remains unclear why the feature was activated or why it did not occur in our environment. In my haste to fix the issue, I failed to fully investigate these details.

To prevent such issues in the future, I plan to implement a notification system that will clearly alert me if such debugging features are active before packaging a version. I will continue to strive to ensure that such problems do not occur again.

notes.title: ver 1.1.0 Update: Adjustments to Basket Capacity Limit
notes.notes:
A critical issue was discovered in this update, resulting in a significant number of customers receiving a build that rendered the game unplayable.

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3313310/view/497182532936139517?l=english

We deeply apologize for the inconvenience caused.
The issue has been resolved in the current version, ver1.1.1.

-------------------------------------------------------
[h1][b]Adjustments to Address Frequent Notifications About Basket Capacity[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318139/404010ab21fb1665d11275ac7bf4dd118c301202.png[/img]

Hello, and thank you for playing Fishing the Abyss!
Today, I’d like to address an issue that some players might have noticed regarding the frequency of notifications about basket capacity. This was a concern I had even before the game’s release.

However, as how players perceive this notification frequency varies from person to person, I decided to wait and see how much feedback I’d receive about this issue after launch.

While the amount of feedback I received was somewhat less than expected, I concluded that it would be worth easing this restriction slightly.

That said, while this game includes idle elements, it is not what you might call a typical idle game that revolves around tracking numerical changes.
I want players to experience the visuals, atmosphere, encounters with creatures, and the events along the limited journey I’ve crafted. The length of idle time can directly affect the richness of that experience.
However, if the intervals are too short, it can interrupt players’ focus on other tasks.

While it’s impossible to create a perfect balance that satisfies everyone, I’m sincerely trying to find a middle ground.

This update aims to adjust that balance.

[h1]Update Details:[/h1]

[h2]■ Slight Increase in Basket Capacity[/h2]

[h2]■ Adjustment to Capacity Growth Based on Basket Levels[/h2]:
Instead of a flat growth rate, early to mid-game capacity will now grow faster, while the growth rate will slow down as players progress into the late game.
This change not only increases the maximum capacity but also makes the effects of capacity growth noticeable earlier in the game.

[h2]■ Reduced Point Multipliers Based on Depth[/h2]:
This adjustment lowers the point multipliers associated with depth. While it might seem like it extends playtime, I’ve paired it with the next adjustment to avoid creating a purely grindy feel.

[h2]■ Adjustment to Point Multipliers Based on Rarity[/h2]:
This adjustment works in tandem with the depth-based multiplier changes to ease the basket capacity limitation while ensuring the game doesn’t feel like it’s artificially dragging out playtime.
As a guideline, creatures with lower rarity will now yield fewer points than before, while higher-rarity creatures will yield significantly more points than before.

In other words, rather than feeling like the basket is always full from repeatedly catching low-rarity creatures, players will enjoy longer idle times in scenarios where only low-rarity creatures are caught. At the same time, catching high-rarity creatures will now accelerate progression more than before and provide a greater sense of satisfaction compared to before. This adjustment aims to create a more dynamic and rewarding experience.
When encountering high-rarity creatures during active gameplay, players will also likely level up as a bonus.
Since actively collecting and spending points during gameplay is unlikely to feel tedious, I’ve shifted the focus of point acquisition towards these moments.

This concludes the adjustments in this update.

It’s possible that some players might still find the intervals too short, while others might prefer the previous experience.
Although it may be difficult to create adjustments that feel perfect for everyone, I hope these changes make the game feel more worthwhile to as many players as possible.

Umaaaaaa
